$comment: Read by an external, project-agnostic tier runner -- not owned by this repo. light runs the tests of the local frontmatter plugin in plugins/note-properties (with its dev dependencies, before the plugin install prunes them), then builds the site the way the production image does (npm ci, plugin install, Quartz's own tests under quartz/ (the plugin's vitest files would break a bare tsx --test), a full quartz build), which is the only check that catches a broken page, a bad wikilink target or a malformed frontmatter block before it reaches the published site; then the contract tests under tests/ (Kubernetes manifests, the image build files and the deploy workflow), and actionlint on the deploy workflow. The full (non-slim) node image is required: the quartz CLI shells out to git at import time and crashes when the binary is missing. stack builds the production image (Dockerfile: Quartz build, then nginx) with a test domain, boots it and probes the routes the site depends on: pages, folder pages, the 404 page and status, sitemap and RSS carrying the rendered baseUrl, the search index and the health endpoint. The runner cannot start the container with a read-only root filesystem; that guarantee is held by the manifest contract tests and the cluster rollout.

light.run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && (cd plugins/note-properties && rm -rf dist && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run typecheck && npm test) && rm -rf .quartz quartz.lock.json && npx quartz plugin install --from-config && npx tsx --test "quartz/**/*.test.ts" "quartz/**/*.test.js" && npx quartz build && npx tsx --test "tests/**/*.test.ts"

probe.run: set -eu; B=http://kb:8080; expect() { c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$B$1"); if [ "$c" != "$2" ]; then echo "FAIL $1: got $c, want $2"; exit 1; fi; echo "ok $1 $c"; }; expect / 200; curl -sf "$B/" | grep -q '<title>'; expect /sitemap.xml 200; curl -sf "$B/sitemap.xml" | grep -q 'https://kb.test.invalid/'; expect /index.xml 200; expect /static/contentIndex.json 200; expect /FRC/FRC-Power/Power-Troubleshooting 200; expect /FRC/ 200; if curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "$B/FRC" | grep -Ei '^location:.*(:8080|http://)'; then echo 'FAIL /FRC redirect leaks port or scheme'; exit 1; fi; expect /no-such-page-xyz 404; curl -s "$B/no-such-page-xyz" | grep -q 404; test "$(curl -sf "$B/healthz")" = ok; echo probe passed
